findings.title: Production fade consumes the first authored door-opening pose
evidence: js/engine.js:808-833 advances EnvironmentReactions before processing fade state.
js/engine.js:827 dispatches ENTITY_ENTERED_DOORWAY while the screen is at full black and immediately begins the 180 ms fade-in.
js/environment-reactions.js:69 defines the first OPENING frame as only 140 ms. It therefore ends before fade-in completes and is mostly obscured in the actual doorway path.
test/environment-entry.js verifies dispatch and eventual CLOSED state, but never asserts which reaction phases are visibly presented during production fade.
The Coldstage contact sheet shows all door poses through direct/manual triggering, which bypasses the production transition timing and cannot catch this integration defect.
findings.resolution: js/engine.js now advances reactions only while fadePhase is zero. The event still commits after successful load/save, but elapsed remains exactly zero throughout fade-in. test/environment-entry.js now asserts elapsed zero during the actual fade, frame 0 for the first 100 visible ms, frame 1 after 160 ms, OPEN after 300 ms, and eventual CLOSED. Independent rerun passed.

findings.title: Published CommonJS setTimeSource export throws
evidence: js/ambient-life.js:132-133 exports setTimeSource outside create(), but its body assigns the create()-local timeSource binding, which is out of scope.
The instance method at js/ambient-life.js:128 works and production uses that method; existing tests do not call the broken module-level export.
findings.resolution: The invalid module-level export was removed. Independent CommonJS probing confirmed that create(seed).setTimeSource(fn) remains functional and the stale surface is absent.

passes: The real door transaction emits only after loadMap and coordinated save succeed; failed-save rollback emits no event.
Direct loadMap and save restoration do not synthesize doorway entry events.
EnvironmentReactions contains no RNG or idle timer; unmatched source/arrival/type events do not start the door.
The registered door follows OPENING, OPEN, CLOSING, CLOSED and coalesces duplicate active events.
Machine activity uses the generic intermittent scheduler with an 8-25 second idle band and configured device-specific marks.
Clock state is mechanically derived from elapsed seconds and supports a pure external time source for future World Time.
Closed reaction draws nothing; permitted evidence shows the final closed frame has the exact static-frame SHA-256.
The environment reaction registry is scene-, trigger-, source-, arrival-, and reaction-identity driven and can register another environment without diner-specific renderer code.
The v0.2 documentation clearly distinguishes continuous, intermittent, and reactive causes and documents the event path and reuse contract.
After re-review, production fade timing preserves the full authored door lifecycle once visible, and the clock's CommonJS instance API is coherent.

The final clock erase mask exactly covers the authored 03:00 hand rectangles at x195/y-7..-4 and x195..197/y-4. The east pendant pool begins at y-4 but its first-row ellipse ends at x194, so these pixels are outside the tint; the remaining tinted face is preserved.

visualEvidence.finding: The machine and clock changes are small and localized. Door frames keep integer, hard-edged pixels and a fixed footprint; closing mirrors opening, and the closed source frame is byte-identical to static. The open doorway is visually severe but coherent with the authored cutaway and does not distort the base raster.

The current frames retain the pendant's warm face tint while clock hands remain crisp; there is no scene-wide movement, altered furniture, or Pass 01 effect drift.
